title: Lanthanocene Diolate Complexes: Synthesis, Structures and Catalytic Property for ε-Caprolactone Polymerization

material_class.structural_family: ionic pinwheel tetramer lanthanocene diolate cluster with μ4-Cl

synthesis.procedure: All manipulations under argon using Schlenk techniques. To a suspension of SmCl3 (0.532 g, 2.07 mmol) in 20 mL THF was added a THF solution of C5H5Na (5.5 mL, 1.13 mol/L, 6.22 mmol) dropwise at room temperature. The mixture was stirred overnight, then a THF solution (ca. 5 mL) of N-phenyldiethanolamine (0.375 g, 2.07 mmol) was added. After stirring for 2 h, the mixture was filtered and the solid extracted completely with THF. DME (5 mL) was added and the solution concentrated under vacuum. Pink powders of 1 formed (0.584 g, 56.6% based on Sm). Crystals suitable for X-ray diffraction were grown from THF–DME at −20 °C.
synthesis.temperature: room temperature for ligand addition; crystallization at −20 °C
synthesis.time: stirred overnight after C5H5Na addition, then 2 h after diolate addition
synthesis.vessel_or_method: Schlenk techniques under argon; filtration and THF extraction
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: filtration; residual solid extracted with THF; 5 mL DME added; concentrated under vacuum to give pink powders; X-ray crystals grown from THF–DME at −20 °C

synthesis.procedure: Prepared analogously to complex 1 under argon Schlenk conditions, substituting YbCl3 for SmCl3: LnCl3 treated first with three equivalents of C5H5Na in THF, then with one equivalent of N-phenyldiethanolamine in THF–DME. Pale-red powders of 2 were obtained (57.9% based on Yb). Crystals for X-ray diffraction were grown from THF–DME at −20 °C.
